correctness.rationale: The exact first-arrival construction and infinite-line half-path equation yield p_infty(t)=exp[-t-2(1-e^-t)]. The backward ancestry can cross distance R only via a strictly decreasing chain bounded by 2^(R+2)/R!. Taking R=ceil(4 log n) makes the total coupling error superpolynomially small. A dependency-neighborhood Stein–Chen bound uses b1,b2=O(log n/n), and factorial moments for well-separated rare edges give the spatial Poisson process. Finally T<=t iff there are zero available edges. Finite-state and randomized verifier completed 71 assertions; computational checks are not a substitute for the analytic argument.

value.rationale: The natural time at which a finite adsorbent loses all admissible dimer sites has a nontrivial extreme-time law on the logarithmic scale. The result identifies its explicit Gumbel centering, positions of the last vacancies as a homogeneous Poisson point process, and an O(log n/n) approximation rate, extending the known mean jamming-coverage calculations into a genuine quantitative kinetic fluctuation theorem.
